الی.note: Uncertain: probably اعلیٰ "most high" (or الٰہی "divine") in a variant spelling.

ہاشم.note: Hashim Shah (c. 1735–1843), author of this Sassi Punnun.

ساتھیں.note: Uncertain: read as a form of ساتھوں "from us".

ہوت.note: Punnun is a prince of the Hot Baloch; "ہوت علی" is his father.

اتے.note: Also the name اتا Atta, the washerman who finds Sassi's chest (oblique اتے).

آدم.en: Adam (Jam Adam, king of Bhambhor); human being

جام.note: Jam is the title of the Sindhi rulers; in "جام صراحی" it means a wine-cup.

خاطر.en: mind, regard; for the sake of
خاطر.note: "خاطر نہ لیاوے" = pays no heed to.

گل.note: Same spelling: گُل gul "flower" (گل بوٹا, گل لالہ); گل gal "neck" (گل لائے, گل بانہہ); گل gall "matter, word".

شام.note: Uncertain: "canopies dark as evening clouds"; شام also means evening.

ہوش.note: "صاحب ہوش دیوانے" = the sane and the mad alike.

ہووس.note: "ہووس اولاد نہ" = that he had no child.

پیر.note: Same spelling for پیر "Sufi saint" and پیر "foot".

آمل.note: Uncertain: read as "آ مل", i.e. that the Lord may come and grant a boon.

در.note: "درِ یتیم" = a peerless pearl; elsewhere در = door.

یتیم.note: Lit. orphan; "dur-e-yatim" = a matchless single pearl.

والی.note: As a noun والی = ruler, lord (شہر دے والی).

ہوتے.note: Uncertain: sense of the line is unclear; possibly "of Hot" (ہوت).

لالہ.note: "گل لالہ" = red tulip/poppy, emblem of a wounded heart.

قدرے.note: "شب قدر", the Night of Power, holiest night of Ramadan.

نوبت.note: Drums played at palace gates on festive occasions.

سروار.note: Uncertain: likely سر وار, gold waved round the head and thrown to the poor.

فقر.note: Uncertain: with اواں likely one word فقراواں "to the poor".

اواں.note: Uncertain: likely second half of فقراواں "to the poor".

جوگی.note: Here جوگا "worthy, able", not the ascetic yogi.

لوکاؤ.note: Uncertain: read as لکاؤ "hiding"; i.e. however much one hides it, who can erase fate.

بھانی.note: "من بھانی" = as his mind held it, frankly.

سو.note: "جو چاہے سو کردا" = whatever He wills, that He does.

بیل.note: The bull of legend that bears the earth on its head.

جا.note: "جا نہ بولن والی" = there is no room to speak.

چین.note: In 20.3 China; in "چین وہاوے" peace, rest.

قسدی.note: Uncertain: possibly کس دی "whose"; the line sets one portion for the wet-nurses.

باشک.note: Mythic serpent who upholds the earth.

دھول.note: In folk cosmology the earth rests on the horn of the bull Dhaul.

ارار.note: "پار ارار" = both banks, from shore to shore.

پہن.note: Uncertain: sense of "پہن لساں چمکاراں" unclear; roughly "the waters flash and glitter".

جلہوڑے.note: Uncertain: some kind of water creature.

زنبور.note: Uncertain in a river list; perhaps a stinging water creature.

چاہ.note: Allusion to the well into which Joseph was thrown by his brothers.

لیتا.note: Uncertain: probably the washerman Atta's name in a variant spelling.

آت.note: Uncertain: "آت باہی" not clear; perhaps "lost, adrift".

دھوبی.note: Sassi is raised by a washerman's family.

بجھاوت.note: Uncertain: likely بجھارت "riddle", i.e. speaking indirectly.

جھڑ.note: Uncertain: phrase "ساک جھڑ وے جیندا" unclear; probably "a match from a lowly line".

یعقوب.note: Jacob wept for his lost son Joseph until he went blind.

ملساں.en: I will meet; will return to

پنوں.en: Punnun, the hero, Baloch prince of Kech

جبرائیل.note: i.e. a peerless artist, a Gabriel among painters.

کوہ.note: "کوہ شکن" = the mountain-breaker, Farhad, lover of Shirin.

ثوابوں.note: Uncertain: "عیب ثوابوں خالی" probably "without any fault".

چڑنگ.note: "put a spark among straw", i.e. set her heart ablaze.

زلیخاں.note: Lover of Joseph (Yusuf), type of the lovesick woman.

ساون.note: "who says they sleep in comfort": lovers never rest

پیالے.note: the cups of love, a Sufi image of intoxicating love

وہاجن.en: to trade, to buy and sell

نیاز.note: Uncertain: nāz-niyāz read as "grace and charm"

یوسف.note: sold into Egypt by a caravan

بھراوا.note: Uncertain: vocative address within the servant's report

الموت.note: part of malak al-maut, the angel of death

مسیحے.note: the Baloch revive her like the Messiah

بنن.note: Uncertain: read as the leader's name

کھٹولا.note: uḍan khaṭolā: a magic flying bed of folk tales

تیوں.note: jiyoṅ jiyoṅ ... tiyoṅ tiyoṅ: the more ... the more

دھائی.note: kar dhāī: hastening; also an attack

چارے.note: jug chāre: the four ages, i.e. forever

پیش.note: pesh nā jāṇā: to be of no avail

وار.note: vār suṭṭṇā: to give up as an offering

لائے.note: sleep does not touch her eyes

جرم.note: Uncertain: "jurm karam": fire of fault and fate

جڑی.note: Uncertain: "prem jaṛī": a root or charm of love

اٹھائی.note: rizq muhār uṭhāī: fate took up the reins

لیجاندے.note: like the caravan that carried Yusuf to Egypt

قہقہہ.note: legendary wall whose viewers laughed and leapt over it

چکور.note: the chakor is said to love the moon

قمری.note: in Persian poetry it laments its love for the cypress

وچارے.note: also bechāre, "poor fellows", in the same verse

فون.note: Uncertain: likely fann, "the art of beloveds"

داغ.note: the tulip's dark heart, a mark of love's wound

دست.note: jo kar dast: folding the hands in entreaty

کن.note: Uncertain: "jin kin": whoever (took) the way of love

خاک.note: putting dust on the head: a sign of mourning

لٹاں.note: loosening the hair: a sign of grief

پرواروں.en: from the halo; from the family
پرواروں.note: the moon escaped its circle of stars

واچے.note: one must live out what fate has written

دھگانے.note: Uncertain: "what blame on whom by force"

پتنگ.note: the moth that dies in the candle flame

تلی.note: life on the palm: ready to die

پرپیر.note: Uncertain: never stepped off her bed before

فرنگوں.note: like release from a Firangi prison

بھٹھیارے.note: her feet roast like grain in a roaster's sand

چمکاں.note: the desert mirage looks like water

خضر.note: the immortal guide who found the water of life

پچھا.note: Uncertain: she turned back to the track

کھر.note: khur khur: melting away like salt

ٹلدی.note: what must happen cannot be averted

کفنی.note: a shroud-like garment worn by ascetics

نابینا.note: as Jacob wept blind for Joseph

باز.note: ishq bāz: those who stake all on love

کچھے.en: from the armpit, at his side

ملیدا.note: a rich treat promised to the camel
